name: Rainline Market
worldBackground: Rainline Market is a neon-drenched street quarter where the rain never quite stops and every puddle doubles the glow of the signs. Noodle bars steam in the dark, a crowded clinic patches up whoever can pay in cash or favors, and families live stacked in old apartment towers above the shopfronts. The tension: the block thrives on its independence, but the clinic's supplies and the market's power both flow through a syndicate that raises its rates a little more each season.

setting.climate: perpetual cool rain, humid, misty nights

templates.name: Serving counter
templates.description: Grease-stained composite counter where noodle bowls, drinks and rationed goods change hands.
templates.physicalDescription: Long steel counter with a scuffed top, holo price tags along the customer edge and a worn staff gap behind.
templates.rule: Every noodle bar, the Static Bar and the bodega get one counter parallel to the entrance wall, staff side toward the back wall.

templates.name: Counter stool
templates.description: Bolted plastic stool for slurpers, drinkers and rumor traders.
templates.physicalDescription: Dented round seat on a single chrome leg, neon reflections pooling in the wet-looking plastic.
templates.rule: A row of stools lines the customer side of each serving counter, spaced one per counter section.

templates.name: Wok range
templates.description: High-BTU noodle station where the night's bowls are flash-fried in steam.
templates.physicalDescription: Blackened twin-wok range with gas lines to a strapped tank, steam haze rising above the burners.
templates.rule: One range against the back wall of each noodle kitchen, beside a wall shelf of ingredient tubs; never in the customer area.

templates.name: Wall shelf
templates.description: Bolted shelving holding bottles, ration tins and wrapped stock.
templates.physicalDescription: Wire shelves crammed with bottles, tins and sealed packs, a cheap strip-light glowing underneath.
templates.rule: Mounted against the back wall behind every serving counter and on clinic walls beside exam beds; never across a door.

templates.name: Refrigeration unit
templates.description: Humming cooler full of drink pouches and synth-meat.
templates.physicalDescription: Frost-fogged glass door stacked with glowing pouches, condensation running to a floor drain.
templates.rule: Stands against a wall beside the serving counter in noodle bars and the bodega; never inside sleeping rooms.

templates.name: Booth table
templates.description: Small bolted table for late bowls, card games and quiet deals.
templates.physicalDescription: Scratched metal table with sticky laminate top, a napkin dispenser and a flickering order tab.
templates.rule: Scattered across Golden Dragon, the Static Bar and the Glass Lotus with a stool beside each, aisles kept wide for tray traffic.

templates.name: Bunk bed
templates.description: Stacked-frame sleeper for capsule drifters and Kowloon Stack families alike.
templates.physicalDescription: Narrow frame with a thin mattress, privacy curtain rail on one side, charger cable and tucked belongings.
templates.rule: One per sleeper against a wall: capsule pods line both sides of the hotel corridor, apartment rooms get one against the far wall.

templates.name: Storage locker
templates.description: Dented personal locker with a keypad nobody trusts.
templates.physicalDescription: Tall steel locker layered in stickers, a faded family photo taped inside the door.
templates.rule: Pushed against walls in apartment rooms, capsule pods and the ripper parlor's tool bay; never blocking a bunk or a bed.

templates.name: Washer machine
templates.description: Communal launderer that eats coins and pumps out gossip with the gray water.
templates.physicalDescription: Row of chipped front-loaders with a detergent shelf above and suds creeping toward the drain.
templates.rule: Wash Cycle lines its washers in rows along the side walls, leaving the center of the laundromat open.

templates.name: Exam bed
templates.description: Patched trauma gurney where Saint Volt stitches the block back together.
templates.physicalDescription: Cracked vinyl pad on a steel frame, blood-pressure cuff coiled at the head, privacy curtain on a bent rail.
templates.rule: Head against the wall in each clinic treatment bay, with a med console within reach of every bed.

templates.name: Implant chair
templates.description: Reclining surgical chair in Doc Grady's back-alley ripper parlor.
templates.physicalDescription: Strapped leather recliner with articulated arm rests, a magnetic tool strip overhead and a drain grate below.
templates.rule: One chair centered in each parlor bay under the surgical lamp, head end toward the wall shelf of tools.

templates.name: Med console
templates.description: Rolling diagnostics stack for vitals, scans and implant firmware.
templates.physicalDescription: Wheeled cart with a green-glowing screen, dangling sensor leads and a taped battery brick.
templates.rule: Stationed beside every exam bed and the implant chair; never in dining rooms, shops or the watch post.

templates.name: Security desk
templates.description: Keystone Watch monitoring desk fed by the block's street cameras.
templates.physicalDescription: Steel desk with stacked screens showing rainy street feeds, a chipped mug and stun baton clips.
templates.rule: Sits inside the watch post facing the door, with the screen wall banked against the far wall.

templates.name: Potted plant
templates.description: Hardy fern that thrives on the damp and ignores the neon glare.
templates.physicalDescription: Chipped ceramic pot with a rain-happy fern, leaves beaded with drift-in moisture.
templates.rule: Clusters at the Glass Lotus door and softens clinic corners; kept off the crowded pavement of Neon Row.

templates.name: Supply crates
templates.description: Syndicate-stamped crates of stock, salvage and contraband.
templates.physicalDescription: Stacked plastic crates with faded stencils, ration bars and battery bricks peeking from the top one.
templates.rule: Stacked behind counters in the bodega and against alley walls; never inside the clinic's queue or treatment space.

templates.name: Vending machine
templates.description: Ration and hot-broth vending unit, card-skimmer included at no charge.
templates.physicalDescription: Graffiti-tagged cabinet glowing with a spiral-noodle hologram, coin slot worn bright.
templates.rule: Butted against shopfront walls beside doors in all three zones, always under a working neon sign.

templates.name: Market stall
templates.description: Tarpaulin stall selling synth-fruit, chargers and knockoff implants.
templates.physicalDescription: Folding frame under striped plastic sheeting, crates of goods displayed and a hanging price holo.
templates.rule: Rows of stalls run along the Neon Row path in front of the shopfronts, leaving the center lane clear.

templates.name: Food cart
templates.description: Wheeled skewer and dumpling cart steaming into the rain.
templates.physicalDescription: Steel cart with a griddle top, gas bottle strapped below, sloped plastic awning shedding water.
templates.rule: Parked beside noodle bar fronts and at Neon Row corners, never inside the clinic block's quiet pavement.

templates.name: Neon arch
templates.description: Tubing arch announcing the market, its glow doubled in every puddle.
templates.physicalDescription: Ribbed arch of multicolored neon on stanchions, open beneath, cables feeding down to a junction box.
templates.rule: One arch spans the Neon Row lane at the street's entrance and one mid-row; never over the clinic or housing lanes.

templates.name: Steam vent
templates.description: Pavement grate belching kitchen steam into the drizzle.
templates.physicalDescription: Rusted grate set in the stone with white steam coiling up, surrounding cobbles slick with condensation.
templates.rule: Set into the pavement beside noodle kitchen walls on Neon Row, never under clotheslines or the clinic queue canopy.

templates.name: Wiring pole
templates.description: Cable-strung pole carrying the block's tapped and tariffed power.
templates.physicalDescription: Leaning pole wrapped in taped cable bundles, a sparking junction box and conduit loops.
templates.rule: Poles line both edges of Neon Row and Stack Alley with cables slung pole to pole above stall height.

templates.name: Fire escape
templates.description: Rusted external staircase zigzagging up the tower face.
templates.physicalDescription: Grated iron stairs and landings bolted to the wall, dripping rails and a rust streak down the stone.
templates.rule: Bolted to the rear and side walls of Kowloon Stack only, never covering windows or street-facing shopfronts.

templates.name: Clothesline
templates.description: Dripping line strung between walkways, washing flapping over the lane.
templates.physicalDescription: Slack cable strung overhead with clipped shirts and sheets, water ticking onto the stones below.
templates.rule: Strung high across Stack Alley between walkway posts and balconies, never across the lane at street level.

templates.name: Drying rack
templates.description: Folding rack sagging with the alley's damp laundry.
templates.physicalDescription: Wire A-frame crowded with drip-hemmed shirts and sheets, shallow puddles spreading beneath.
templates.rule: Racks sit in the sheltered gaps under Stack Alley's dripping walkways, clear of the fire escape's drip line.

templates.name: Dumpster
templates.description: Syndicate-locked waste hauler that residents pay twice for.
templates.physicalDescription: Dented green dumpster with a smart-lock lid, runoff streaking toward a clogged drain.
templates.rule: Tucked behind buildings in Stack Alley beside service doors, never on the market street or near the clinic queue.

templates.name: Queue canopy
templates.description: Clear-plastic shelter where the hurt wait their turn at Saint Volt.
templates.physicalDescription: Ribbed translucent shelter on stanchions, taped floor guides beneath, rain sheeting off the edges.
templates.rule: One canopy in front of Saint Volt Clinic over the bench queue line, never covering the drone pad.

templates.name: Streetlight
templates.description: Rain-haloed light pole with a scrolling ad panel bolted on.
templates.physicalDescription: Slim pole with a rain-diffused glow, an ad strip crawling with loan offers, reflections below.
templates.rule: Lights line the paths of all three zones, on Neon Row spaced opposite the wiring poles.

templates.name: Drone landing pad
templates.description: Marked pad where med-drones land with syndicate-billed supplies.
templates.physicalDescription: Painted circular pad with a glowing landing ring, guide lights and a cable to a charger post.
templates.rule: A single pad on the open edge of Clinic Block beside the clinic, kept clear of canopies and overhead cables.

templates.name: Bench
templates.description: Slatted bench for queuing, recovering and whispered favors.
templates.physicalDescription: Steel-slat bench with rain beading on the seats, a stripped ad frame at one end.
templates.rule: Benches line the Clinic Block paths under the queue canopy and face the teahouse; none along Neon Row's eating stretch.

templates.name: AC unit
templates.description: Dripping heat exchanger bolted where the towers breathe.
templates.physicalDescription: Rusted fan-box with a condensation drip line and cable taped up the stone.
templates.rule: Bolted against the outside walls of Kowloon Stack and above shop back doors, never on the Neon Row street front.

npcs.name: Mei-Lin Zhou
npcs.description: She keeps twelve tables boiling past midnight on a syndicate power line that costs more every season, and she wants to buy her own generator before the spring rate hike; she worries her stuttering coolant unit will spoil a whole week of broth in one warm night.
npcs.physicalDescription: Broad-shouldered and quick, in an oil-stained apron over a padded rain jacket, with a pale steam-burn scar across her left forearm that she scratches when counting the till.

npcs.name: Ruben Alkaev
npcs.role: bartender and rumor-broker at Static Bar
npcs.description: He trades drinks for gossip behind the bar's ten flickering taps and wants to buy the bar's debt note out from under the syndicate; he worries the two Keystone men who drink for free are memorizing every name he says.
npcs.physicalDescription: Lean and restless, in a rolled-sleeve shirt and knit cap pulled low over the data-jack behind his ear, polishing the same glass for an hour at a stretch.

npcs.name: Suri Pham
npcs.description: She counts every battery and water chit twice at her counter and wants to lock a direct synth-food supply run before syndicate couriers squeeze her shelves empty; she worries her rationed-water contract will be 'renegotiated' the way the noodle bars' power was.
npcs.physicalDescription: Small and quick-moving, in layered thermals under a vendor's slicker, with a price-gun on a wrist lanyard and chipped red nail polish she never redoes.

npcs.name: Tamsin Okafor
npcs.role: night nurse at Saint Volt Clinic
npcs.description: She triages whoever can pay in cash or favors under the clinic's four treatment canopies and wants an independent line on antibiotics that doesn't pass through syndicate warehouses; she worries about the night the grid browns out while eight wounded are still on her tables.
npcs.physicalDescription: Tall and hollow-eyed from double shifts, in clinic-green scrubs under a soaked rain shell, with glow-tape strips wound around her boot soles for blacked-out corridors.

npcs.name: Ivo Grady
npcs.role: back-alley implant surgeon at Doc Grady's Ripper Parlor
npcs.description: He installs and patches street implants at his single swivel-mounted chair and wants to clear the loan that bought his surgical arm before the syndicate claims the parlor itself; he worries his aging sterilizer unit is one failed cycle from costing a patient an infection.
npcs.physicalDescription: Heavyset and stooped over his tools, in a stained technician's smock, with a surgical magnifier band pushed up on his forehead even when he's eating.

npcs.name: Ansel Reyes
npcs.description: He minds the laundromat's nine humming machines and collects the block's gossip with its lint, wanting to stay politely invisible; he worries a Keystone man will finally ask him directly what the noodle cooks say about the rate hikes.
npcs.physicalDescription: Stooped and mild, in a buttoned cardigan and fingerless gloves, pushing a folding cart of other people's forgotten socks down Stack Alley every evening.

npcs.name: Li-Wen Chao
npcs.role: keeper of the Glass Lotus Teahouse
npcs.description: She pours six varieties of steeped tea at her four calm recovery tables and wants the teahouse to stay neutral ground where clinic families and syndicate men drink side by side; she worries the season's price war will turn her quiet corner into just another contested doorway.
npcs.physicalDescription: Silver-braided hair coiled tight, in layered gray robes that never quite dry, with a faintly glowing jade implant at her temple that blinks when she suppresses a remark.

npcs.name: Dane Volkov
npcs.role: shift captain at Keystone Watch Post
npcs.description: He runs the six-guard rota that keeps the block quiet for the syndicate and wants his skimming of the tariff ledgers to stay buried one more quarter; he worries the new regional auditor will pull the watch post's camera archives the way he pulled the noodle bar's power logs.
npcs.physicalDescription: Slab-shouldered and deliberate, in a gray tactical coat with the Keystone badge freshly sewn on, with cracked plating across two knuckles he flexes before conversations.

npcs.name: Kex Marlow
npcs.role: street runner and drone wrangler on Neon Row
npcs.description: She runs noodle orders, spare parts and unmarked parcels along the market's fourteen stall rows and wants to buy her capsule contract out of the hotel by year's end; she worries a syndicate collection drone will flag one of the parcels she didn't open.
npcs.physicalDescription: Short and always half-jogging, in a reflective tarp poncho cinched with cargo cord, with three ear studs that are actually signal antennas she checks by touch.

npcs.name: Guan Yee Ho
npcs.description: Everyone calls her Auntie Ho, and she grills synth-eel skewers at her corner stall two doors from the noodle bars, wanting to keep her grandson out of Keystone's guard roster; she worries her propane permit will be 'reviewed' the way every independent stall's has been.
npcs.physicalDescription: Round-faced and iron-gripped, in three sweaters under an oilcloth apron, with a bamboo fan she snaps open at anyone who lingers without buying.

player.name: Emil Varga
player.description: An outsider whose cargo rig was impounded at the Keystone Watch Post pending a 'weather tariff' he can't pay, he works nights at Grady's parlor repairing med-drones to earn his release fees, and he wants his rig free before the winter monsoon grounds all freight for good; he worries the syndicate will discover what's actually in his sealed cargo pods before he does.
player.physicalDescription: Pale from too many cockpit years, in a weatherproof field jacket with frayed cuff seams, with a gloved cyberhand missing two fingertips he never bothers to replace.

frame.premise: Three blocks of a leased city: the corps own the buildings, the fixers own the favours, and the chrome in your arm is still on its payment plan.
frame.conflict: The lease on your chrome is being called in, and the repossession clock does not care who you owe first
frame.playerRole: a courier whose eyes and left arm are leased from a ripperdoc
constraints: No clean getaways: every deal costs something visible
frame.summary: The district runs on Keystone scrip and borrowed chrome. By day the noodle bars and laundromats do honest trade; by night the Static Bar brokers the favours that keep the clinics paid. The player is a courier whose leased eyes and left arm are three payments behind, and Doc Grady has started the repossession clock: seventy-two hours until the chrome comes back out. Everyone in the three blocks owes someone, and most of them owe each other - which makes every favour a lever and every friend a risk. The corps count everything; the streets count back.
unresolved: what Keystone wants with the clinic's pickup file

narrativeRules: Everything leaks: rain, data and intentions.
Nobody works for free; name the price in the first scene.
The clock ticks in every downtown scene: say the hours left.
Chrome is collateral: it can be broken, never ignored.
The Watch logs everything it sees and sells half of it.
Violence is fast, loud and expensive afterwards.
